title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54 — Lecture 8: Ricardian Trade Model (Fall 2016)
use: Primary instructor method route for unit-labor production, opportunity costs, specialization, incomplete-specialization boundaries and competitive wages. The chapter independently constructs and clears its two-country examples and proves the feasible-budget comparison.
verification: Retrieved the actual 21-page official MIT PDF; inspected extracted body text on physical PDF pages 4–13 and17–20. This includes assumptions, production constraints, autarky/trade specialization, endpoint cases and wage relations. The source's numerical illustration and diagram artwork were not reproduced. The chapter does not generalize homogeneous-factor gains to all households in richer economies. No contemporary trade facts were drawn from the source.

title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54 — Lecture 13: Heckscher–Ohlin Model of Trade I (Fall 2016)
use: Primary instructor method route for factor mobility within a country, unit-cost equations, factor-market clearing and conditional factor-price equalization. The chapter's fixed-coefficient production and dual supporting-price proof are original specializations.
verification: Retrieved the actual 19-page official PDF and inspected extracted body text on physical PDF pages 3–7 and14–18. The inspected content includes zero-profit/resource systems, the requirement that both goods be produced, and a fixed-proportions illustration. The chapter supplies different technologies, endowments, consumption closure, numerical values and a complete global supporting bound; it does not copy the source's mixing example or infer universal factor-price equalization.

title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54 — Lecture 14: Heckscher–Ohlin Model of Trade II (Fall 2016)
use: Primary instructor method route for relative endowments, common technologies/preferences, specialization limits and the Stolper–Samuelson real-reward mechanism. The original chapter proves only its explicitly bounded fixed-coefficient case and computes actual ownership transfers.
verification: Retrieved the actual 16-page official PDF and inspected extracted body text on physical PDF pages 3–9 and13–15, including conditional diversification, the relative-abundance trade prediction and the differentiated zero-profit real-reward argument. A screenshot request was made but no visual-inspection claim is made here; review relied on actual extracted PDF text and the chapter's independent algebra. No empirical inequality assertion or unrestricted general theorem is imported.

title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54 — Lecture 17: Increasing Returns to Scale (Fall 2016)
use: Primary instructor method route for internal versus external scale economies, fixed costs, declining average cost, residual demand and the comparison of positive-operation profit with staying out.
verification: Retrieved the actual 25-page official PDF and inspected extracted text on physical PDF pages 3–14 and17–24. The chapter uses only the scale/profit-choice method and the warning that residual demand depends on competition. It derives its own finite destination-profit function, global branch proof and example. The source's free-entry industry model, variety welfare and country-integration comparative statics are not claimed as solved by the chapter's conditional export model.

title: Arnaud Costinot, MIT 14.54 — Lecture 18: Consequences of Increasing Returns, Theory and Evidence (Fall 2016)

verification: Retrieved the actual 22-page official PDF and inspected extracted body text on physical PDF pages 14 and17–19 for heterogeneity, cost cutoffs and trade-cost mechanisms.
